# Architecture — Web (apps/web)

*Generated by the BMad document-project workflow — deep scan, 2026-07-17.*

## Executive Summary

`apps/web` is Telar's cockpit — a Next.js 16 (canary) App Router application that is simultaneously the UI and the HTTP host for `@telar/core`, the loom engine. There is no separate backend service: `packages/core` is consumed as TypeScript source in-process (`"@telar/core": "workspace:*"`, `exports["."] → "./src/index.ts"`, no build/publish step), called directly from React Server Components, Route Handlers, and `apps/web/instrumentation.ts`.

The app has two structural halves:

1. **App Router pages** (`app/**/page.tsx`) — mostly `"use client"` components that fetch JSON from the app's own API and render the cockpit (dashboard, loom list/detail, project hub, settings). A few pages (`app/looms/plan/[project]/page.tsx`, `app/projects/[name]/sessions/[id]/page.tsx`, `app/settings/page.tsx`) are (or start as) React Server Components that call `@telar/core` functions like `getProject`/`listAccounts` directly, with `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"` so the registry/manifest is always read fresh.
2. **API route handlers** (`app/api/**/route.ts`) — 56 `route.ts` files, 70 HTTP method handlers total, every one of them calling into `@telar/core` or an `apps/web/lib/*` bridge on top of it. There is no `pages/api`, no `"use server"` Server Actions anywhere in the tree, and no `middleware.ts` — this is a local, single-user cockpit that trusts the caller (see Conventions & Constraints).

The centerpiece is `POST /api/chat` (`apps/web/app/api/chat/route.ts`, ~1,900 lines): one agent-turn endpoint that runs either the Claude Agent SDK's `query()` or a Codex `app-server` JSON-RPC bridge (`apps/web/lib/codex-app-server.ts`), streams ~17 named Server-Sent-Event types back to the browser, wires in-process MCP tool servers for the loom and Ultra subsystems, and structurally enforces the "human always accepts" rule via a `PreToolUse` hook that force-routes `mcp__loom__start_loom` and `mcp__loom__answer_blocked` through an interactive permission card in *every* SDK permission mode — an agent literally cannot start or resume a loom without a human clicking accept.

For the full request/response contracts of every route, see [./api-contracts-web.md](./api-contracts-web.md). For persisted/wire data shapes, see [./data-models-web.md](./data-models-web.md). For the component tree, see [./component-inventory-web.md](./component-inventory-web.md). For the engine this app hosts, see [./architecture-core.md](./architecture-core.md).

## Architecture Pattern

**In-process monolith, App-Router-as-backend.** `apps/web` is not a thin client of a separate API service; it *is* the service. Route Handlers under `app/api/**` import `@telar/core` functions directly and run them in the same Node process as the page renderer (confirmed by `next.config.ts`'s `transpilePackages: ["@telar/core"]`, which tells Next to compile the workspace package's TS source rather than expect a prebuilt `dist/`).

Two sub-patterns compose this:

- **Server-rendered shell, client-fetched data.** Nearly every interactive screen (`app/page.tsx`, `app/looms/page.tsx`, `app/looms/[id]/page.tsx`, `app/projects/page.tsx`, `app/projects/[name]/page.tsx`) is a `"use client"` component that renders a skeleton, then `fetch()`s its own `/api/*` routes on mount and on a `telar:refresh` custom-event / polling interval. This keeps `@telar/core`'s Node-only code (fs, child_process, the Agent SDK) out of client bundles — client components only ever import *types* from `@telar/core` (erased at build time), never its runtime code.
- **Thin server components for first paint.** A few routes (`app/looms/plan/[project]/page.tsx`, `app/projects/[name]/sessions/[id]/page.tsx`) are `async function` Server Components that call `getProject`/`listAccounts` from `@telar/core` directly, pass only plain serializable data as props into a client component (e.g. `SessionView`), and mark themselves `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"` so the on-disk registry/manifest is never stale from a cached RSC render.

**Streaming.** Two SSE consumption patterns coexist, both hand-rolled (no `EventSource` polyfill library, no `ai` SDK's `useChat`):
- `POST /api/chat` returns a raw `ReadableStream` of `event: <name>\ndata: <json>\n\n` frames; the client reads it with `res.body.getReader()` and `apps/web/lib/sse.ts`'s `consumeSSE()` — a hand-written frame parser shared by every consumer of this wire format (chat turns *and* the mini-dock's live tail).
- GET-based tail endpoints (`/api/looms/[id]/events`, `/api/chat/[sessionId]/events`, `/api/ultra/[id]/events`) are consumed with the browser's native `EventSource`, since they're simple long-lived GETs with no request body. `app/looms/[id]/page.tsx` still layers a 2s poll of the loom itself on top of its `EventSource` subscription as a deliberate resilient fallback — an in-process build agent can hog the same Node event loop the SSE write pump runs on, so the poll catches state changes the stream missed. It opens a second, independent `EventSource` when a woven child Thread's drawer is open.

**In-process MCP tool servers.** `apps/web/lib/loom-mcp.ts` and `apps/web/lib/ultra-mcp.ts` each build an MCP server object (via the Agent SDK's in-process server support) exposing loom/Ultra-lifecycle tools (`start_loom`, `answer_blocked`, `draft_bundle_file`, …) directly to the SDK's `query()` call inside `POST /api/chat` — no separate MCP process, no stdio/socket transport for these two servers.

**No auth layer.** No `middleware.ts`, no session cookie, no API key check anywhere in `app/api/**`. Any process that can reach the port can call any route. This is a deliberate scope choice for a local single-user desktop/CLI-launched cockpit (see `scripts/telar`, `apps/desktop/main.js`), not an oversight to "fix" in isolation — see Conventions & Constraints.

## Entry Points

| Entry point | Path | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Root layout | `apps/web/app/layout.tsx` | Wraps every route: fonts (Geist/Geist Mono), pre-paint theme-init `<script>`, `ThemeProvider`, `LoomNotifications`, `DockProvider` → `SidebarProvider` → `AppSidebar` + page content, portaled `Dock` |
| Dashboard page | `apps/web/app/page.tsx` | `"/"` — the command-center screen (see Module Overview screen table below) |
| Server boot hook | `apps/web/instrumentation.ts` | Next's `register()`, run once per server instance before it accepts requests; dynamically (Node-runtime-guarded: `if (process.env.NEXT_RUNTIME !== "nodejs") return`) imports `@telar/core` and calls `reconcileStuckLooms()` to recover looms left mid-flight by a prior crash |
| Build config | `apps/web/next.config.ts` | `transpilePackages: ["@telar/core"]`; `distDir` overridable via `NEXT_DIST_DIR` (lets a prod build coexist with an always-on dev server); `output: "standalone"` gated behind `NEXT_OUTPUT=standalone` for desktop packaging |
| API entry | `apps/web/app/api/**/route.ts` | 56 files, 70 handlers — see the summary table below |
| CLI launcher (external) | `scripts/telar` | Starts this app detached under `~/.telar/launcher/`, opens the browser — the normal way a human starts the cockpit |
| Desktop shell (external) | `apps/desktop/main.js` | Forks this app's standalone build (`NEXT_OUTPUT=standalone`) as a child process, points an Electron `BrowserWindow` at it |

## Data & State

**No global client state library.** The app deliberately uses plain React state + a small number of hand-rolled external stores instead of Redux/Zustand/Jotai/SWR/React Query (none are dependencies):

- **Server truth, client-polled.** Most screens hold `useState`/`useEffect` + `fetch()` against the app's own API, refetching on mount, on a `window` `"telar:refresh"` custom event (broadcast by mutating actions elsewhere in the tree), and on a 5s `setInterval` while something is actively running (e.g. `app/page.tsx`'s `hasActive` poll). This is the dominant pattern across `app/page.tsx`, `app/looms/page.tsx`, `app/projects/page.tsx`.
- **`lib/ui-prefs.ts`** — a `useSyncExternalStore`-based store for theme, default model/permission-mode for new sessions, and notification toggles, persisted to `localStorage` under `telar-ui-prefs` with cross-tab sync via the `storage` event. Explicitly UI-preference-only: "Nothing writes telar.yaml / .telar or any engine env."
- **`components/dock/dock-provider.tsx`** — a `createContext` store for the mini-dock (sessions that follow the user across routes). Durable identity (`DockEntry`: id/title/project/auto-docked flag) persists to `localStorage` (`telar:dock-entries`, `telar:dock-viewed`); live state (messages, working/parked flags, cost) is never stored — each docked session independently re-fetches/re-tails the same HTTP surface a standalone session page would (`GET /api/chats/[id]`, `EventSource` on `/api/chat/[sessionId]/events`, `POST /api/chat` to send).
- **`components/ai-elements/prompt-input.tsx`**'s `PromptInputProvider` — a third app-level `createContext` store (alongside `DockProvider` and the shadcn/base-ui `SidebarProvider`) that lifts the composer's text value so `SessionView` and the slash-command menu share one source via `usePromptInputController()`.
- **Server-side, file-backed persistence** (not client state, but what the client ultimately reads through the API): `apps/web/lib/store.ts` owns `~/.telar/chats.json` (chat transcripts) and `~/.telar/usage.ndjson` (append-only usage ledger) — "files remember; no database." `apps/web/lib/permissions.ts` owns `~/.telar/permissions.json` (per-project always-allow rules). `@telar/core`'s own state (`telar.yaml` per project, the loom store, MCP OAuth tokens) is a separate persistence domain the web app never touches directly on disk — always through `@telar/core`'s own read/write functions.

**Streaming state.** In-flight turn state (`ReadableStream` of SSE frames from `POST /api/chat`) is parsed by `session-view.tsx` via `consumeSSE()` and folded into local component state as it arrives (`text`, `tool`, `tool_result`, `thinking`, `delta`, `thinking_delta`, `permission`, `task_status`, `done`, …). `POST /api/chat` runs are **not** bound to the request/response lifecycle — an `AbortController` registered in `lib/chat-runs.ts` keeps a turn running server-side even if the client disconnects; a reconnecting client (or the dock) tails the same turn via `apps/web/lib/session-log.ts`'s append log + delta ring rather than losing state on navigation.

Full persisted/wire type definitions (`Chat`, `ChatMessage`, `Part`, `UsageEntry`, `Loom`, event payload shapes, etc.): [./data-models-web.md](./data-models-web.md).

## Testing Strategy

**Unit tests: colocated, Bun-native.** Every `*.test.ts` file sits next to the module it tests (not in a separate `__tests__/` tree) and runs under `bun test` (`bun:test` imports, e.g. `import { afterAll, describe, expect, test } from "bun:test"`). There is no test script wired in `apps/web/package.json` — tests run via the root Bun toolchain, consistent with this repo's own `telar.yaml` gate (`{name: test, run: "bun test"}`).

| File | Lines | Covers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lib/permissions.test.ts` | 612 | Rule derivation (`ruleFor`), guardrail decisions, pending-approval lifecycle, protected-path checks |
| `lib/ultra-mcp.test.ts` | 303 | Ultra MCP tool server behavior |
| `lib/transcript.test.ts` | 297 | Tool-input/output capping, subagent parent-flattening |
| `lib/loom-mcp.answer-blocked.test.ts` | 234 | `answer_blocked` tool path (M11.3 escalation resume) |
| `lib/commands.test.ts` | 195 | Slash-command registry |
| `lib/titles.test.ts` | 159 | Session-title generation |
| `lib/loom-mcp.remint.test.ts` | 127 | Loom MCP session "remint" behavior |
| `lib/m11-discuss-first-turn.test.ts` | 117 | Escalation-kickoff first-turn framing |
| `lib/gallery-fixtures/fixtures.validate.test.ts` | 388 | Structural validation of demo-gallery fixture scenarios |

No React component-level tests exist (no `@testing-library/*`, no Jest, no `*.test.tsx`) — coverage is concentrated on `lib/` business logic, not rendering. `@playwright/test` and `@playwright/mcp` are present as **devDependencies but are not imported anywhere in `apps/web` source** (confirmed by search) — they exist so the packaged Verifier (an `@telar/core` agent that drives a real browser to check a running app) has `@playwright/mcp` available at runtime; `apps/desktop/build-web.sh` explicitly copies this package into the standalone build for that reason. They are not a web-app UI test framework.

`scripts/e2e/greenfield-next/` (outside `apps/web`) exercises the whole cockpit end-to-end by running a scripted "greenfield Next.js project" through a real loom lifecycle — this is the closest thing to an integration test for this app's API surface, but it lives at the repo-tooling level, not inside `apps/web`.

## Integration Points

- **`apps/web` → `packages/core`** — `"@telar/core": "workspace:*"` in `apps/web/package.json`; Bun workspaces resolve it to `packages/core`, whose `exports["."]` points straight at `./src/index.ts` (no compiled `dist/`). `next.config.ts`'s `transpilePackages: ["@telar/core"]` makes Next compile that TS source directly. Consumed from: nearly every `app/api/**/route.ts`, `app/looms/plan/[project]/page.tsx`, `app/projects/[name]/sessions/[id]/page.tsx`, `instrumentation.ts`, `lib/loom-mcp.ts`, `lib/ultra-mcp.ts`. 112 `from "@telar/core"` import statements across the app source (excluding the `.next-desktop/` build-output copy, which must never be counted as source); the most-imported symbols are `getProject`, `getLoom`, `listAccounts`, and `loadPolicy` — i.e. project/manifest reads and account lookups dominate, consistent with nearly every route needing to resolve a project or account before doing anything else.
- **`apps/web` → `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`** — `POST /api/chat`'s Claude branch calls `query()` directly with a `canUseTool` callback (the interactive permission card), a `PreToolUse` hook (the loom-moat guardrail), and in-process MCP servers from `lib/loom-mcp.ts`/`lib/ultra-mcp.ts`.
- **`apps/web` → Codex `app-server`** — `POST /api/chat`'s Codex branch (provider `"codex"`) shells out to the `codex app-server` JSON-RPC process via `lib/codex-app-server.ts`, normalizing its stream into the *same* `send()` event vocabulary (`session`, `text`, `thinking`, `tool`, `tool_result`, `done`, `saved`, …) and reusing the exact same permission-card machinery (`createPending`/`resolvePending` from `lib/permissions.ts`) for interactive approvals — so the client-side composer/renderer needs zero provider-specific branching.
- **`apps/web` ← `apps/desktop`** — `apps/desktop/build-web.sh` runs `next build` inside `apps/web` with `NEXT_OUTPUT=standalone NEXT_DIST_DIR=.next-desktop`, producing `apps/web/.next-desktop/standalone/apps/web/server.js`, which `apps/desktop/main.js` forks as a child process and points a `BrowserWindow` at.
- **File-backed state under `~/.telar`** — `apps/web/lib/store.ts` (`chats.json`, `usage.ndjson`) and `apps/web/lib/permissions.ts` (`permissions.json`) own their own files there, alongside (but independent of) whatever `@telar/core` itself persists (per-project `telar.yaml`, the global project registry, MCP OAuth tokens). `TELAR_HOME` env var can relocate the home dir (used by `bun dev`'s script and by tests).
- **No external API dependency for its own operation** beyond whatever the active account's provider (Claude/Codex CLI login) and any project's configured MCP servers require — git/GitHub integration (`app/api/projects/[name]/git/**`) shells out to local `git`/`gh` via `@telar/core`'s `vcs.ts`, not a hosted API client.

## Conventions & Constraints

- **`apps/web/AGENTS.md` (read via `apps/web/CLAUDE.md`) is load-bearing**: *"This is NOT the Next.js you know. This version has breaking changes... Read the relevant guide in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` before writing any code."* Because the app runs a Next.js **16 canary**, do not assume stable-Next-15 App Router APIs are unchanged — verify against `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` or the actual behavior in this repo before relying on training-data knowledge of Next.js conventions.
- **Client-bundle rule (enforced by convention, not tooling)** — client (`"use client"`) modules must import only *types* from `@telar/core` (erased at build time), never its runtime code, since the package pulls in `fs`, `child_process`, and the Agent SDK. Server-only helpers are isolated under `lib/server/`. `lib/permission-modes.ts` exists specifically as a client-safe split-out of the permission-mode constants from `lib/permissions.ts`, which itself imports `./loom-mcp` → the Agent SDK and cannot be bundled for the client. The rule is self-documented with in-file comments at each boundary rather than enforced by an ESLint rule or bundler check — see e.g. `components/common/loom-notifications.tsx`, `components/looms/blocked-escalation.tsx`, `components/looms/utils.ts`, `components/projects/git-tab.tsx`, and `components/session/session-view.tsx`, each of which calls out "CLIENT-BUNDLE RULE" or `import type` only in a header comment; `instrumentation.ts` states the reason directly ("the `@telar/core` barrel pulls in Node-only modules (fs, child_process, the agent SDK)").
- **Route nesting mirrors resource hierarchy exactly** — e.g. `app/api/projects/[name]/git/remote/issues/[number]/comment/route.ts` — rather than flattening into query params on a single handler.
- **Every `route.ts` file uses the App Router "Route Handler" convention**: `export async function GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE(...)`. No arrow-function exports, no `pages/api`, no Server Actions (`"use server"`) anywhere in `apps/web`.
- **No auth/authz layer**: no `middleware.ts`, no session or API-key check. This cockpit is designed to be started locally (`scripts/telar`) or packaged into a single-user Electron shell (`apps/desktop`), not exposed as a multi-tenant service — any feature work that would expose this app beyond localhost needs an explicit auth design, which does not currently exist.
- **The loom-acceptance moat is structural, not a UI convention**: `mcp__loom__start_loom` and `mcp__loom__answer_blocked` are force-routed through the interactive `canUseTool` permission card by the `PreToolUse` hook in `app/api/chat/route.ts` *regardless of the session's chosen permission mode* (`default`/`auto`/`acceptEdits` — see `lib/permission-modes.ts`; the SDK's own `bypassPermissions`/`dontAsk`/`plan` modes are never accepted from a client request, enforced by `isValidPermissionMode`). There is no code path — auto-mode, "always allow" rule, or otherwise — that lets an agent start or resume a loom without a human clicking the card. Any new tool with comparable "commits real work" semantics should follow this same pattern rather than relying on `permissionMode` alone.
- **File writes are atomic**: `lib/store.ts` and `lib/permissions.ts` both write to a `.tmp` file and `fs.renameSync` over the target, never a direct in-place write — required reading before touching either module's persistence logic.
- **Escalation kickoff (`lib/escalation-kickoff.ts`)**: when a human clicks "Discuss with the orchestrator" on a blocked loom (`discuss-escalation.tsx`), `SessionView` only mounts *after* that click, then auto-fires exactly one hidden first turn whose wire `message` is an opaque sentinel (`ESCALATION_KICKOFF_SENTINEL`) — no user chat bubble is rendered, so the agent appears to "speak first." `app/api/chat/route.ts` recognizes the sentinel (`isEscalationKickoff`: role `"escalation"`, no `sessionId` yet, message === the sentinel) on a brand-new escalation session and substitutes the real instruction (`ESCALATION_KICKOFF_PROMPT`) before the model ever sees the sentinel, so a human could never type it by accident and reach the kickoff branch. This module is pure and dependency-free specifically so both the client (`session-view.tsx`'s `shouldFireEscalationKickoff`) and the server (`route.ts`'s `isEscalationKickoff`/`resolveEscalationMessage`) share one source of truth for the contract, unit-tested in `lib/m11-discuss-first-turn.test.ts`. The resulting proposal still only executes through the human-approved `answer_blocked` tool — this module never bypasses the accept moat above, it only shapes the first turn's framing.
- **`chats.json` is rewritten whole on every `appendTurn`**, which is why `app/api/chat/route.ts` enforces `MAX_DETAILED_TOOL_PARTS = 200` (tool parts beyond that per-turn ceiling degrade to name-only) — a deliberate bound to stop one pathological turn from blowing up the synchronous full-file rewrite that every other chat's save also pays for.
- **Protected/off-limits paths for this documentation effort and for general repo hygiene**: `.next`, `.next-desktop`, `node_modules`, `release/` are build/tooling output and must never be read as source of truth — `apps/web/.next-desktop/standalone/apps/web/**` in particular contains a *copy* of this app's source (including `*.test.ts` files), which `bunfig.toml`'s `[test].pathIgnorePatterns` explicitly excludes from `bun test` discovery so they never run as if live.
- **`components.json`** configures the shadcn component generator (component paths, Tailwind config location) — new UI primitives should be added via that generator's conventions, landing in `components/ui/`, not hand-rolled from scratch.

## API Surface at a Glance

56 `route.ts` files, 70 HTTP method handlers, grouped by resource. Full request/response contracts: [./api-contracts-web.md](./api-contracts-web.md).

| Resource group | Base path | Methods present | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Chat (live turns) | `/api/chat`, `/api/chat/stop`, `/api/chat/permission`, `/api/chat/[sessionId]/events`, `/api/chat/[sessionId]/watches` | POST, GET, DELETE | The agent-turn SSE endpoint, its stop/interrupt, interactive permission-card answer, session tail/reconnect, and file-watch subscriptions |
| Chats (persisted history) | `/api/chats`, `/api/chats/[id]` | GET, PATCH, DELETE | Chat list (with preview) and single-chat CRUD (rename/archive/delete) |
| Looms (lifecycle) | `/api/looms`, `/api/looms/[id]`, `/api/looms/[id]/{accept,reject,cancel,resume,steer,chat,threads,events,spec,spec/[...path],evidence/[...path],charter/approve,block/answer}` | GET, POST | The full scope→orchestrate→build→verify→(repair)→ready→accept→done HTTP surface. `accept` is the **only** accept endpoint and requires a human-originated request — no agent-callable accept exists anywhere in the tree |
| Ultra (parallel-run harness) | `/api/ultra`, `/api/ultra/[id]`, `/api/ultra/[id]/{agents/[ordinal],events,resume,stop}` | GET, POST | CRUD + SSE event tail for the deterministic Ultra script harness (`packages/core/src/ultra/`) |
| Projects (registry) | `/api/projects`, `/api/projects/[name]`, `/api/projects/[name]/{commands,mcp}` | GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE | Project registration/manifest CRUD, per-project slash-commands, per-project MCP server config |
| Git integration | `/api/projects/[name]/git`, `/api/projects/[name]/git/{cleanup,files,remote,remote/issues,remote/issues/[number],remote/issues/[number]/{comment,state},remote/prs/[number],remote/prs/[number]/{comment,files}}` | GET, POST | Local git status/branches/worktrees + GitHub remote issues/PRs (read + comment/state) |
| Accounts | `/api/accounts`, `/api/accounts/[name]`, `/api/accounts/[name]/login` | GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE | Claude/Codex account registry CRUD + interactive login flow |
| MCP OAuth | `/api/mcp/oauth/{connect,callback,status,disconnect}` | GET, POST | OAuth connect/callback/status/disconnect for MCP servers requiring auth |
| Permissions | `/api/permissions/[project]` | GET, DELETE | Read/clear a project's persisted "always allow" rule set |
| Usage | `/api/usage` | GET | Telar-recorded request, token, and cost summary |
| Models | `/api/models` | GET | Available model/effort option catalog |
| Doctor | `/api/doctor` | GET | Machine environment/dependency health check |
| Browse | `/api/browse` | POST | Filesystem browse helper (project-root picker) |

**SSE-streaming endpoints**: `POST /api/chat` (raw `ReadableStream`, hand-parsed), `GET /api/chat/[sessionId]/events`, `GET /api/looms/[id]/events`, `GET /api/ultra/[id]/events` (native `EventSource`-compatible).
